questions.question_text:
A triangle has an area of $40\text{ cm}^{2}$, one side of length $10\text{ cm}$, and an included angle of $30^{\circ}$.
What is the length of the other side forming this angle?

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the area formula.
Divided the area by the side length without accounting for sine or halving.
Multiplied by $2$ instead of dividing by $\sin 30^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
A triangle has an area of $48\text{ cm}^{2}$, a side of $12\text{ cm}$, and an included angle of $60^{\circ}$.
What is the length of the other side, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Omitted the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ when setting up the area formula.
Computed $48 / 6$ but forgot to divide by $\sin 60^{\circ}$.
Multiplied by $\sin 60^{\circ}$ instead of dividing by it.

questions.question_text:
A triangle has an area of $30\text{ m}^{2}$, one side of length $8\text{ m}$, and an obtuse included angle of $150^{\circ}$.
What is the length of the other side?

options.why: Omitted the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the area formula.
Divided the area by the side without using the angle.
Multiplied by $2$ instead of dividing when solving for $b$.

questions.question_text:
A triangle with sides $7\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ has an area of $21\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, what is the size of $\theta$?

options.why: Evaluated $\cos^{-1}(0.5)$ instead of $\sin^{-1}(0.5)$.
Gave the obtuse supplementary angle despite the acute condition.
Assumed $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ without computing the ratio.

questions.question_text:
A triangle has sides of $8\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ and an area of $24\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is obtuse, what is the size of $\theta$?

options.why: Stated the acute angle instead of the obtuse supplement $180^{\circ} - 60^{\circ}$.
Confused $\sin 120^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ with $\sin 150^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Selected the $45^{\circ}$ obtuse partner instead of the $60^{\circ}$ partner.

questions.question_text:
A triangle has sides of length $5\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$ and an area of $18\text{ cm}^{2}$.
What are all possible sizes for the included angle $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree?

options.why: Omitted the obtuse supplementary solution $180^{\circ} - 53^{\circ} = 127^{\circ}$.
Omitted the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the area formula, calculating $\sin\theta = \frac{18}{45} = 0.4$.
Evaluated $\cos^{-1}(0.8)$ instead of $\sin^{-1}(0.8)$.

questions.question_text:
An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of $30^{\circ}$ and an area of $18\text{ cm}^{2}$.
What is the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Computed $\sqrt{36}$ by omitting the $\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5$ term.
Divided $72$ by $6$ instead of taking the square root.
Halved $8.5\text{ cm}$ or made an algebraic arithmetic error.

questions.question_text:
A triangle has sides of $6\text{ m}$ and $8\text{ m}$ and an area of $12\sqrt{2}\text{ m}^{2}$.
What are the two exact possible values for the included angle $\theta$?

options.why: Failed to recognise the obtuse supplementary solution $180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ}$.
Evaluated $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
Evaluated $\sin\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

questions.question_text:
An isosceles triangle with equal sides of length $x$ has an apex angle of $120^{\circ}$ and an area of $18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^{2}$.
What is the exact value of $x$?

options.why: Omitted the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ from the area formula, giving $x^{2} = 36$.
Computed $x^{2} = 72$ but forgot to take the square root.
Made an arithmetic error when simplifying $\sqrt{72}$.
